Morocco have climbed two places to fifth in the latest FIFA Men’s World Rankings, matching the highest position Nigeria has ever held in the standings. The Atlas Lions have 1,809.37 points in the rankings released on Wednesday. They are the first African nation to enter the top five since Nigeria reached the same position in April 1994, a gap of 32 years. Their rise followed two wins over Niger in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers during the November international break. Morocco won the first game 5-1 and the return fixture 1-0 on Tuesday. The 17-year-old Abdellah Ouazane scored the only goal in the second match, handing Morocco their fourth straight win in Group A and confirming their place at the 2027 AFCON. They have taken all 12 points from their four qualifiers, with two games left. Spain remain on top of the rankings, followed by Argentina, France and England. Portugal and Brazil have dropped to sixth and seventh, respectively. FIFA ranking: Super Eagles rise one place to 29th globally 2027 AFCON: Nine countries secure qualification FULL LIST: Teams leading AFCON 2027 qualifying groups Morocco are among nine countries that have secured places at the 2027 AFCON after the fourth round of qualifiers. They are joined by Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso, Benin and Cameroon, while co-hosts Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda qualified automatically. Burkina Faso beat Mauritania 3-1, Mali won 2-0 against Rwanda, and Cameroon went through after Comoros defeated Congo 1-0. Senegal’s qualification was confirmed by results elsewhere. The tournament will run from June 19 to July 17, 2027, with the remaining 15 places to be decided when qualifying ends in March 2027. The Super Eagles moved up one place to 29th globally and are fifth in Africa with 1,564.18 points. Eric Chelle’s men beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo last Friday but drew 0-0 in Zanzibar on Tuesday. The result lifted them above Algeria, who dropped four places to 32nd and sixth in Africa. Senegal are second in Africa and 18th in the world, followed by Egypt (26th) and Côte d’Ivoire (28th).
